<title>feat(cast/selectors): show function state mutability</title>
<body>## Motivation
The new version of EVMole can extract function state mutability with [high accuracy](https://github.com/cdump/evmole?tab=readme-ov-file#function-state-mutability). Let's use it in `cast selectors`

## Solution
Upgrade EVMole to 0.4.1 and show state mutability in the `cast selectors` output

```
$ cast selectors $(cast code 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2)
0x06fdde03                              view
0x095ea7b3      address,uint256         nonpayable
0x18160ddd                              view
0x23b872dd      address,address,uint256 nonpayable
0x2e1a7d4d      uint256                 nonpayable
0x313ce567                              view
0x70a08231      address                 view
0x95d89b41                              view
0xa9059cbb      address,uint256         nonpayable
0xd0e30db0                              payable
0xdd62ed3e      address,address         view

$ cast selectors $(cast code 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2) --resolve
0x06fdde03                              view            name()
0x095ea7b3      address,uint256         nonpayable      approve(address,uint256)
0x18160ddd                              view            totalSupply()
0x23b872dd      address,address,uint256 nonpayable      transferFrom(address,address,uint256)
0x2e1a7d4d      uint256                 nonpayable      withdraw(uint256)|OwnerTransferV7b711143(uint256)
0x313ce567                              view            decimals()
0x70a08231      address                 view            balanceOf(address)
0x95d89b41                              view            symbol()
0xa9059cbb      address,uint256         nonpayable      transfer(address,uint256)
0xd0e30db0                              payable         deposit()
0xdd62ed3e      address,address         view            allowance(address,address)
```

According to [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#resolving-an-issue), I've used Cargo nightly, Cargo fmt added `;` to some existing return statements in `crates/cast/src/lib.rs`
```
$ cargo +nightly version
cargo 1.83.0-nightly (c1fa840a8 2024-08-29)

$ cargo +nightly fmt -- --check && cargo +nightly clippy --all --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings && echo OK
...
OK
```</body>

<title>fix: watch less files.</title>
<body>Some users are running into "too many watched files" errors.
Mainframe has already had its watch limits raised to 1m.
Think i've identified a few troublesome folders. This PR tells vscode to stop watching so many files.
You can get an idea of how many files you're watching (on linux) using:
```
grep inotify /proc/*/fdinfo/* 2>/dev/null| wc -l 
```

This took me from 90k to about 10k after restarting vscode server (not sure if i needed to kill the server, but think i did).
To kill server run in your sysbox (save and quit vscode first):
```
pkill -f '.vscode-server'
```</body>

- On-chain - Domain-based [21 patterns]
  Definition: On-chain patterns that implement domain features (BPM, identity, big data, and features reusable across domains). The SLR treats this as an intermediate category under On-chain pattern, intended to grow as new domain-specific patterns appear.
  Source: Six et al. 2022, §4.1 and §4.2.2
  Subcategories: BPM; Decentralized identity; Big data; Multi-domain feature
- On-chain - Smart contract [24 patterns]
  Definition: Patterns about implementing and managing smart contracts: how contracts are organized together, secured, made cheaper to execute, and how function access is authorized.
  Source: Six et al. 2022, §4.1 and §4.2.3
  Subcategories: Contract management; Contract security; Contract efficiency; Contract access control
- On-chain - Data management [13 patterns]
  Definition: Patterns for efficient management of data that already live on-chain, in smart contracts or transactions. Distinct from the On/off-chain 'Data management' subcategory, which keeps the payload off-chain and only uses the chain for integrity or trust.
  Source: Six et al. 2022, §4.1 and §4.2.4
  Subcategories: Storage; Encryption; Migration; Tokenization
- Architectural [3 patterns]
  Definition: Architectural patterns about who creates and signs blockchain transactions (user, browser wallet confirmation, or a delegated service). The SLR places them outside the design-pattern taxonomy proper because only three were found; this working catalog keeps them as a first-class category.
  Source: Six et al. 2022, §4.2.5
  Subcategories: (no subcategory; patterns sit directly under the category)
- Idiom [5 patterns]
  Definition: Solidity idioms that reduce execution fees by packing storage, choosing integer/mapping layouts, or freeing unused slots. The SLR found no dedicated idiom papers but classified 14 such items separately from design patterns; this catalog keeps them as a category.
  Source: Six et al. 2022, §3.4 and §4.2.5
  Subcategories: (no subcategory; patterns sit directly under the category)

response_json_schema.description: Gate de categorias SLR: decide quais ramos da taxonomia merecem triagem de patterns, sem nomear o pattern ainda.

issue_summary.description: Resumo técnico curto do tema real do artefato, sem inferir código ausente.

issue_activity_type.description: Tipo principal de atividade do próprio artefato.

issue_challenge_categories.description: Desafios explicitamente discutidos no nível da issue; use none_explicit quando não houver.

context_status.description: Se o texto disponível é suficiente para o gate de categoria.

categories.description: Uma entrada por categoria canônica do catálogo, inclusive as irrelevantes.

relevant.description: yes somente com evidência positiva parcial de discussion de pattern nesse ramo.

evidence_text.description: Trecho literal se relevant=yes; vazio se relevant=no.

evidence_location.description: Local do trecho, ou string vazia se relevant=no.

rationale.description: Por que o ramo passa ou falha no gate.

confidence.description: Confiança no gate de categoria, não no pattern final.
